title: White v. Siouxlands Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. The SJC held that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in denying the complaint and sent the matter back to Presbytery with instructions to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence holds or is preaching/teaching views on the Covenant of Works or other doctrines associated with the so-called Federal Vision theology that are contrary to the PCA doctrinal standards. Concurrence agreed in result; dissent would have afforded greater deference to Presbytery.
first_summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Siouxlands Presbytery for refusing to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister's Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. It held that Presbytery applied too high an evidentiary standard at the investigation threshold and remanded for the investigation. A concurrence agreed in result but criticized the majority's unnecessary reasoning; a dissent argued the matter was discretionary and deserved great deference absent clear error.
summary: A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion.

sources.supports: Canonical case identity, issue, judgment, adopted reasoning, concurrence, dissent, and voting lineup.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2008-14, White v. Siouxlands Presbytery, decided by the Standing Judicial Commission at the 38th General Assembly (2010). The opinion was written by TE David Coffin and amended by the full SJC; 22 concur, 1 dissent, 1 absent (ll. 1-3, 225-229).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s denial of a request to appoint a committee to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into TE Greg Lawrence’s alleged Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views (ll. 13-33, 69-79; printed pp. 135-138).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC sustained the complaint; it held Presbytery erred and remanded with instructions to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation (ll. 35-37, 223). The adopted reasoning distinguishes the BCO 31-2 investigation threshold from BCO 35 conviction evidence standards: credible injurious reports, including hearsay, can trigger investigation, and conflicting testimony can make investigation more imperative (ll. 97-225; printed pp. 139-144).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The concurring opinion agrees in result but objects to the majority’s unnecessary argument and relies on BCO 39-3.3 clear error (ll. 231-261). The dissenting opinion argues the matter is one of discretion and judgment deserving great deference, that no clear error was shown, and that the majority did not clearly define the threshold standard (ll. 263-550). These are separate opinions, not adopted reasoning.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference. The dissent’s reference to 2009-05 Payne v. W. Carolina is illustrative only and not part of the adopted judgment (l. 362).

source_limits: The source is the SJC decision and its separate opinions. It does not include the full Record of the Case, party briefs, or any subsequent proceedings. The facts are as summarized in the SJC opinion, and the dissent’s proposed CS-CW standard and deference analysis are not adopted.
benchmark_examples: C01: preserve mixed outcomes, procedural error, and remand rather than collapsing into a single result.
C02: distinguish investigation from censure and keep adopted reasoning separate from concurrence or dissent.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged action: Presbytery’s refusal to order a BCO 31-2 investigation.
score_reasons.decision: States the complaint was sustained and the matter remanded, while noting concurrence and dissent.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted BCO 31-2 investigation threshold and the error of applying BCO 35 conviction standards.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the rule that credible injurious reports, including hearsay or conflicting testimony, can trigger investigation without establishing guilt.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the majority’s adopted reasoning from the concurrence and dissent and avoids treating proposed standards as holdings.
score_reasons.economy: All retained details explain the dispute, result, or doctrinal/procedural value of the case.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative judgment at ll. 35-37 and 223, the adopted reasoning at ll. 97-225, the concurrence at ll. 231-261, and the dissent at ll. 263-550. Corrected the first summary to state the BCO 31-2 investigation trigger and to avoid presenting the dissent’s CS-CW/deference analysis as the majority holding. Confirmed the complaint was sustained and remanded, not merely reversed, and that no separate relief beyond remand was granted.
